summary: PAPER-LIU-WOOD-ZUREICKBROWN-24 extracts Liu–Wood–Zureick-Brown, A predicted distribution for Galois groups of maximal unramified extensions (Invent. Math. 237 (2024) 49–116), read as arXiv v2. It has 45 items (42 missing, 2 planned, 1 library), seven routes and 29 source issues. Its routes hold against RS-17 and RS-29, and the accepted ArithmeticStatistics blueprint already carries out route 4 and imports route 2 as intended. Both Part IIs are consistent: one coalesces with WOOD-19's. Four findings, all low. (1) Item 10's note says a pro-odd 𝓕_n avoids Feit–Thompson, which is the reverse of the truth. (2) Item 43 claims ProfiniteProPGroups Layer 4 plans the paper's pro-𝒞 completions, but those are Γ-equivariant level-𝒞 completions, not extension-closed classes, and item 1 already owns them. (3) The prerequisites omit Bertin–Romagny and Romagny–Wewers, which §11 uses. (4) There is no sourceVersions list, though the collation worklist does track the paper.
checked: Independence: the extraction is by Claude Code cc-39fac3 and its review by Claude Code cc-442dc5. This worker (Claude Code, cc-c2c06b) did neither, and did not work on the ArithmeticStatistics blueprint.

The repository at 141d3145: the extraction, its review and review JSON, the ArithmeticStatistics packet, and the extractions it shares machinery with: WOOD-19, ELLENBERG-VENKATESH-WESTERLAND-16 and CHEN-24. The assembled atlas has 2840 stages and 8007 edges. All ten cited stage ids exist. Restructurings accepted before the review: IG.3 and IG.4 were narrowed by RS-29, and DWP.7 by RS-17. IG.3 still keeps braid/Hurwitz actions on Nielsen classes (route 3). IG.4 keeps finite embedding problems with local constraints, supplied by ProfiniteProPGroups Layer 5 (route 1). DWP.7 keeps the H_c upper weight bound (item 44). IG.5, ST.5, SF.2 and EDC.2:pairings are kept, and GN.4 is unchanged.

Routes 4 and 2 against the blueprint. The accepted ArithmeticStatistics blueprint (#2864) already has ST.5 nodes for route 4's Lemma 9.3, Theorem 1.4 and Corollary 1.5. It imports IG.5 for Lemmas 10.2–10.3 and Theorem 10.4, as route 2 intends, and it cites route 7's Part II for Theorem 6.2. E6, E7 and E28 are re-recorded there as ArithmeticStatistics/E672–E674, marked known with the extraction's ids, so nothing is recorded twice.

Part IIs. Route 6 coalesces with PAPER-WOOD-19's route 8: the same id, InductionRestrictionPartIIReducedSchur, and the same title, whose first half is the current title of the Tau Ceti roadmap InductionRestriction. Route 7's title reproduces ArithmeticStatistics' current title. No other extraction routes random Γ-groups, level-𝒞 completions or profinite Schur–Zassenhaus. EVW16's abelian moment-uniqueness items go to ST.0/ST.5, a different statement.

Statuses at Mathlib 082e2d3 and Tau Ceti f790474. All eight Mathlib names that item 45 cites exist. Tau Ceti has only the braid-group presentation (TauCeti.BraidGroup), with no Hurwitz action or Nielsen classes. Neither library has profinite Schur–Zassenhaus or free pro-C groups. ProfiniteProPGroups plans neither Schur–Zassenhaus nor conjugacy of complements, so item 10 is rightly missing.

Source issues. I re-derived E7's counterexample: x³ − 4x + 1 has discriminant 229; h(Q(√229)) = 3, and the fundamental unit (15 + √229)/2 has norm −1, so this is the only totally real S_3-field with rDisc 229, against N = |Aut S_3| = 6. I also re-derived E12's Z/4 example (Y(G) = {0, 2}), E8's a = (1, 0) example and E25's n = 0 edge case. I did not re-verify E5 (Property E) or E6 beyond reading their arguments. Prerequisites: checked against the arXiv v2 bibliography and the places where §§2–12 cite it (finding 3).

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-LIU-WOOD-ZUREICKBROWN-24.result.json: item /10 (Schur–Zassenhaus for profinite groups), note; read with item /4's note
findings.claim: Item 10's note ends: 'When Γ is solvable, or 𝓕_n is pro-odd, no Feit–Thompson is needed.' The second half is false. 𝓕_n is pro-|Γ|′, so it is pro-odd exactly when |Γ| is even. Conjugacy of complements is known when the normal subgroup or the quotient is solvable. An odd-order group is solvable only by Feit–Thompson, so the pro-odd case is exactly where Feit–Thompson is needed, unless Γ happens to be solvable. The paper says as much on p. 17: 'when |Γ| is odd, our random groups are not necessarily pro-solvable.' When |Γ| is even they are pro-solvable, and that is Feit–Thompson. The error matters here. Item 4's note correctly says that Theorem 1.4's hypotheses force |H| odd. Read together, the two notes suggest that Theorem 1.4 can be formalized without Feit–Thompson for any Γ.
findings.evidence: Item 10 note: 'The general conjugacy statement uses the Feit–Thompson theorem (one of the two coprime orders is odd) or a solvability hypothesis. … When Γ is solvable, or 𝓕_n is pro-odd, no Feit–Thompson is needed.' Item 4 note: 'The hypotheses force |H| odd (q or q − 1 is even).' arXiv v2 (SHA-256 7f1e85da…, the extraction's file), p. 17, end of §3.2: 'We remark that, when |Γ| is odd, our random groups are not necessarily pro-solvable.' Mathlib at 082e2d3 has existence for finite groups (Subgroup.exists_right_complement'_of_coprime, SchurZassenhaus.lean:277) and conjugacy only for an abelian normal subgroup (Subgroup.exists_smul_eq, :103). The accepted ArithmeticStatistics blueprint therefore states LWZB Lemma 9.3 and Theorem 1.4 under an explicit hypothesis (SZ), 'all sections of H ⋊ Γ → Γ are H-conjugate'. It discharges (SZ) only for abelian H (ST.5/complements-of-a-coprime-abelian-normal-subgroup-are-conjugate).
findings.fix: Replace the last sentence of item 10's note with: 'Without Feit–Thompson, conjugacy is available when Γ is solvable or when the groups H in question are solvable (abelian, nilpotent, or pro-p as in §7). An odd-order H is solvable only by Feit–Thompson. The ArithmeticStatistics blueprint therefore states Lemma 9.3 and Theorem 1.4 under the hypothesis (SZ).'

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-LIU-WOOD-ZUREICKBROWN-24.result.json: item /43 (free profinite groups and pro-p presentations), statement, status planned and note; compare item /1
findings.claim: Item 43 is planned at ProfiniteProPGroups Layers 4–5 for 'free pro-|Γ|′ groups on finite sets and their pro-𝒞 completions'. Layer 4 plans pro-C completions only for a FiniteGroupClass. That is a class of finite groups, with no Γ-action, that must be closed under extensions: the layer rules out nilpotent groups for that reason. The completions this paper takes are level-𝒞 completions (𝓕_n)^𝒞, as item 1 defines them. There 𝒞̄ is closed only under finite products, Γ-subgroups and Γ-quotients, and everything is Γ-equivariant. Most of the paper's 𝒞 are not extension-closed, among them the p-Γ-groups of p-class ≤ c in Theorem 7.5 and the groups of order ≤ ℓ in §5. Only two cases fall under Layer 4: the pro-|Γ|′ completion that builds F_n, and the pro-p completion of §7.2. Item 1 already carries the level-𝒞 completion, as missing on route 7, so item 43 claims a planned supplier for something that route 7 must build.
findings.evidence: Item 43 statement: 'Free pro-|Γ|′ groups on finite sets and their pro-𝒞 completions.' Note: 'The upstream ProfiniteProPGroups roadmap plans free pro-p and pro-𝒞 groups on finite sets for a structured class 𝒞 (Layer 4; the prime-to-|Γ| groups form such a class).' Layer 4 in the assembled atlas: '`proCCompletion C G := G ⧸ proCKernel C G` … Every pro-`C` statement below is about this structure'; 'The class of finite nilpotent groups is **not** an example: it is not closed under extensions'. Item 1: 'For a set 𝒞 of finite Γ-groups, 𝒞̄ is its closure under finite products, Γ-subgroups and Γ-quotients, and G^𝒞 = lim G/M over closed normal Γ-subgroups with G/M ∈ 𝒞̄'. Item 28 (Theorem 7.5) and item 22 (𝒞_ℓ, the |Γ|′-Γ-groups of order ≤ ℓ) use such 𝒞.
findings.fix: Restrict item 43 to free pro-|Γ|′ and free pro-p groups on finite sets (with the Γ-action on F_n(Γ) by permuting generators, which is functoriality in the generating set) and to pro-p presentations. Add: 'Level-𝒞 completions of Γ-groups are item 1 (route 7), not Layer 4.'

findings.claim: The prerequisites list Wewers's thesis and Hall's relative GAGA for §11. They omit the two other Hurwitz-space sources that §11 relies on. §11 opens: 'We refer to [BR11] for general facts about Hurwitz spaces.' The definition of Hur^n_G (item 30) takes étaleness of the branch locus from [BR11, Proposition 3.1.1]. §11.3, which builds the topological Hurwitz space of item 31, says 'we model our arguments on [RW06, Section 3]'. The atlas does not cover either source: no extraction, packet or papers.json entry cites Bertin–Romagny or Romagny–Wewers. The other sources in §11 are Keel–Mori, Rydh, Olsson, Knutson, Artin 1970 and the Stacks Project. Those are foundations of stacks, algebraic spaces and coarse spaces, which SF.1, R09.3, R09.5 and ComplexComparisonPartII:C3 plan, so their omission is within §16's rule.
findings.evidence: arXiv v2, p. 41: 'We refer to [BR11] for general facts about Hurwitz spaces.'; 'the properties that D → S is étale [BR11, Proposition 3.1.1]'. p. 44: '11.3. Topological Hurwitz spaces. … we model our arguments on [RW06, Section 3]'. Bibliography: '[BR11] José Bertin and Matthieu Romagny, Champs de Hurwitz, Mém. Soc. Math. Fr. (N.S.) 125–126 (2011)'; '[RW06] Matthieu Romagny and Stefan Wewers, Hurwitz spaces, in Groupes de Galois arithmétiques et différentiels, Sémin. Congr. 13, Soc. Math. France (2006), 313–341'. At this revision, grep finds 'Romagny' in no file under research/blueprint/papers or research/blueprint/packets, and no stage description in the assembled atlas mentions either work. PROTOCOL §16: '`prerequisites` lists the papers this one builds on that the atlas does not yet cover'.
findings.fix: Add both to prerequisites. Bertin–Romagny, Champs de Hurwitz, Mém. SMF 125–126 (2011), doi 10.24033/msmf.437: 'general facts on Hurwitz stacks; Proposition 3.1.1, the branch locus of a tame Galois cover is étale over the base (item 30)'. Romagny–Wewers, Hurwitz spaces, Sémin. Congr. 13 (2006) 313–341: '§3, the topological Hurwitz space that §11.3 follows (item 31)'.

The file has no sourceVersions list. What was read is recorded only in readSections and in each finding's 'searched' text. The collation worklist does list this paper, with 6 statements on a preprint and the publisher blocking fetching. So the §18 safeguard is working here, and this is bookkeeping only. It is the same gap as in the red teams of Koymans–Milovic and DeMarco–Krieger–Ye.
